item: Cause of the frequency and radar problems
note: Officials say telecom outage but haven't named the failed system or carrier. CBS, citing multiple sources, reports a network update caused a reboot; that is not officially confirmed.

item: Confirm the CBS network-update/reboot report with the FAA or DOT
note: Checked 7:22 PM ET: not confirmed. FAA and DOT still call it only a telecommunications or communication outage, with technicians investigating. CBS cites unnamed multiple sources. Bloomberg cites one person saying the FBI is looking at a software update and doesn't believe it was a cyberattack. L3Harris has made no statement.

item: Which specific frequencies or channels went down
note: None named publicly; a unique Reagan National tower failure remains unconfirmed

item: Airband recordings or spectrum captures from SDR communities
note: None found; LiveATC archives are blocked from my computer, though the Chicago feed names are known

item: Domestic ground stop lifted
note: At 8:23 PM ET the FAA status summary no longer lists the national stop, but there is no lift advisory or FAA statement, and AP still says it runs through at least 11 PM ET. American says some airports are getting clearances.

item: Outcome of the 9:15 PM ET planning webinar
note: The FAA national summary lists the next planning webinar at 0215Z (9:15 PM ET).

item: Outcome of the 7:15 PM ET planning call
note: No restart came out of it: at 7:44 PM ET the FAA still lists the national stop until 11 PM and set the next planning webinar for 9:15 PM ET.

item: Whether the Newark PENNS restriction clears with the national stop
note: Still active at 7:21 PM ET and listed until midnight, one hour past the national stop's 11 PM end. Official FAA text is STOP ZOB to EWR via PENNS 2234-0500 EQ:FAA (Cleveland Center traffic arriving at Newark via PENNS, not Newark departures); requested by ZNY and provided by ZOB, started 5:34 PM ET. Still listed at 7:44 PM ET. Consistent with a Cleveland-specific constraint but not proof of a second fault; recheck after 11 PM ET.

item: What "communications failure" means in practice
note: The FAA reason changed from "telecommunications outage" to "COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE" without naming the system, circuits or carrier

item: Rumor that AT&T provides the ARTCC network
note: Partly true at most. AT&T won the FENS contract in Aug 2026, but the only funded work is a $74.3M planning task order. L3Harris still operates FTI. No recent public document names AT&T as a current FTI circuit provider, and nothing public links AT&T to today's outage.

item: Rumor that 911 systems are also down
note: Unconfirmed. No FCC, carrier or 911-center confirmation of a nationwide outage. Downdetector logged user reports from 4:13 PM ET (unverified, likely including panic reports) and a separate overnight spike (peak 298 at about 5:21 AM ET). Lincoln, NE and Tulare, CA lost only non-emergency lines; Lincoln-Lancaster EMA said 911 was working.

item: Any SMART link to the outage
note: CISA is reviewing; no evidence so far. Air Space Intelligence denies SMART caused it. Officials have not established a role.

item: Chicago as the starting point
note: First in the FAA paperwork, confirmed. Whether the failure technically started there is still unclear.

item: L3Harris copper-to-fiber changeover as the cause
note: The 70% upgraded figure is confirmed. A cutover causing today's outage is unverified: no public schedule or contract change names Nov. 13, and L3Harris says it cuts over in low-traffic windows.

item: Cleveland Center equipment hold on Newark arrivals
note: Most likely the same national failure (medium confidence). No separate advisory in the 70–123 range. Official FAA restrictions list: STOP ZOB to EWR via PENNS 2234-0500 EQ:FAA — Cleveland Center traffic arriving at Newark via PENNS, not Newark departures. Requested by ZNY, provided by ZOB, 5:34 PM–midnight ET. Earlier Newark stops were for volume and ended before 3:10 PM.

item: The two areas that kept communicating
note: Mullin said two US areas were unaffected and would not name them. Inference, medium confidence: Alaska and Hawaii, based on Alaska Airlines' statement that intra-Alaska and Neighbor Island flights were not impacted. No FAA advisory carves them out.

item: Cyberattack
note: No public evidence; not officially ruled out. CISA and the FBI have made no public statement. Mullin would not rule it out. NBC and Bloomberg, citing officials, say early signs point away from cyber.

item: Kansas City Center as the origin, and Reagan National
note: The Kansas City origin is a rumor, contradicted by the Chicago-first advisories. No ZKC-specific advisory. Reagan National held under the national stop is confirmed. A unique tower failure is unconfirmed.

item: Why the Weather Service radar site went down
note: Debunked as a separate outage. Stale webpage text; NWS says radar is operating normally.

item: Canadian systems hit
note: Not hit, per NAV CANADA and Transport Minister MacKinnon. Only US-bound flights, and some flights crossing US airspace, were stopped.

item: Airport weather radar dropouts tied to the same network
note: Boston Center's teleco issue was cited when Boston's radar data came back at 3:46 PM.

item: Public carrier outage ruled out for the window
note: No public AT&T or Verizon consumer outage lines up with the window. L3Harris runs the private FTI network and had no comment.
